newsitem.title: USA: US House panel chair gunning at Clinton - Democrats.
newsitem.headline: US House panel chair gunning at Clinton - Democrats.

text.p: Minority Democrats on the House committee investigating campaign fund raising charged the committee chairman with running a one-man partisan probe aimed at President Bill Clinton.

A letter from all 19 Democrats and one independent on the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee complained to Republican chairman Dan Burton he was running an unfair probe that included subpoenas unrelated to fund raising, such as doctor visits involving the Clintons.

The letter that was made public was prepared by ranking Democratic member Henry Waxman, a California Democrat, who said Democrats wanted bipartisan cooperation but were left out of decision-making by Burton, an Indiana Republican.

"Unfortunately, without seeking the approval of the committee, you have implemented procedures that are unfair to the minority and have established a bipartisan scope and budget for the investigation," the letter said.
The letter was the culmination of a series of complaints from Waxman that escalated with all other 19 minority members joining him in the letter complaining about the progress of the investigation.
Besides Burton's committee, the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee headed by Tennessee Sen. Fred Thompson is investigating the mushrooming funds affair.
Neither committee has held hearings yet and both have been going over subpoenaed documents. Thompson's committee is not expected to hold public hearings until mid or late May.

The Democratic said Burton unilaterally decided to release documents to the media without consulting the committee, had decided on his own to issue subpoenas without consultation and presented a $3.8 million investigative budget aimed strictly at Clinton and Democrats.
"The unilateral authority that you assert to release committee documents, including privileged and confidential documents, is an extraordinary and unprecedented power," the letter said.
On the subpoenas, the committee under Burton's orders has issued 46 subpoenas but the Demcorats charged that some have nothing to do with the pending investigation.

"The unilateral subpoenas you have issued compel the production of extraordinary sensitive national security and foreign policy documents that have no apparent connection to any alleged fund-raising abuse," the letter said.

"The subpoenas also would require the production of purely personal information about the Clintons ... as well as copies of confidential Democratic political strategies developed as a legitimate part of the last presidential campaign," the letter-writers said.

The Democrats and independent Bernard Sanders of Vermont said the chairman has long had power to issue subpoenas unilaterally but noted it was not done that way when Democrats headed the committee. Instead, the Democrats asked for a committee vote or agreement of subpoenas from the ranking minority member.
A spokesman for Burton said that after getting the letter he has decided tentatively to hold a committee meeting next Wednesday to discuss the grievances.
